source.title: Beyond Components: Singular Vector-Based Interpretability of Transformer Circuits
source.authors: Areeb Ahmad; Abhinav Joshi; Ashutosh Modi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether individual orthogonal singular directions within transformer components carry distinct functions, using SVD-based decomposition, learned masks, and directional interventions rather than the original toy-network setup.
record.gate_note: The paper studies pretrained GPT-2 Small, not toy networks with a controlled excess of sparse features. It does not test feature sparsity or importance transitions, neuron-level capacity competition, SAE feature recovery or canonicality, or whether model features are multi-dimensional. Its main relevant evidence is for task-specific functions associated with individual singular directions and interventions on those directions. Mask visualizations and other qualitative claims are described in the paper but are not exhaustively transcribed here; numerical and explicitly quantified results are prioritized.
record.test_reason: The paper says components are 'superpositions of orthogonal subfunctions', but it means rank-1 SVD terms of weight matrices in GPT-2 Small. These are orthogonal by construction and no more numerous than the matrix rank. It never measures features outnumbering dimensions, interference, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features, or whether features are 1-D rather than multi-dimensional. Its results concern which weight-matrix singular directions matter for IOI, GT and GP, and what they appear to do. That is a related but different construct, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that heads and MLPs are not monolithic but multiplex several low-rank subfunctions along orthogonal singular directions, which align with known IOI circuit heads. They also claim scalar interventions on gender OV directions causally control pronoun prediction, which they say flips 'with perfect accuracy' at high amplification. They note limits: GPT-2 Small only, matrices analysed independently, and causal mediation not fully established. Their word 'superposition' means co-located orthogonal subfunctions, not more features than dimensions.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes pretrained GPT-2 Small weight matrices with SVD, learns masks over singular directions, and performs selected scalar interventions; it does not reproduce the toy-network setup described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction masks and retained functions depend on task/dataset; the GP intervention effect varies with amplification scale and whether all or only gender-specific directions are swapped.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, sparse subsets of orthogonal singular directions in attention/MLP weight matrices preserve task behaviour (IOI ~91%, GT/GP >95% of directions pruned). Single heads (9.6, 9.9, 10.0, 9.1, 6.9) contain several directions with distinct apparent roles, e.g. start-of-sequence detection, entity/action separation and entity salience. Swapping gender-direction scalars with amplification flips pronoun predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual attention heads and MLPs carry multiple functionally distinct low-rank weight-space directions (intra-component multiplexing). This differs from activation-space feature superposition.

record.problems: The experiments use one model, GPT-2 Small (124M parameters), and selected benchmark tasks. The authors note that independently analyzing matrices may miss cross-component interactions, that interpretability and causal relevance of singular directions are not formally justified, and that their output-faithfulness mask objective does not by itself establish end-to-end causal mediation. Some all-head evidence is presented in figures without tabulated values.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted additional directions and qualitative analyses from §§5 and B.3–B.5, including head 9.9/10.0 descriptions, head 5.5 results, and figure-only all-head mask visualizations. Prioritized tabled numerical results and explicitly quantified findings; Table 6 duplicates the scale-20 intervention summaries in Table 5 and was not duplicated.

untested.parts: All: no toy model, no sparsity sweep, no features-versus-dimensions excess, no geometry.
All: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity-allocation analysis.
All: no analysis of where polysemantic neurons come from.
All: no measure of features spread across neurons and no SAE. The SVD directions are orthogonal, rank-bounded weight bases.
All: rank-1 SVD terms are imposed by the method. No comparison with multi-dimensional features, no test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'tests' link and both V6 labels are unfounded. One-dimensionality is built into the SVD method, not tested. The record's limits_scope label was also based on untested parts, which the rules exclude. All rows relinked to none. Mask values (R50-R52) are selection outputs, and Table 1 evaluates the authors' own method.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-model sweep over feature count, dimension, feature sparsity, interference, or regular geometry.
No test of neuron polysemanticity caused by capacity pressure, or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions while others share.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure.
No measure of features spread across neurons or of sparse features recovered with an SAE.
No test of SAE features as complete, stable, canonical model units.

Tests functional roles associated with one-dimensional singular directions in GPT-2 Small components; does not compare against an alternative account in which the underlying features are intrinsically multi-dimensional.
